desc: Prove/disprove the lemma that an optimal sequence flips each index at most once; if false, identify the correct structural property (e.g., extra flips can reduce cost by lowering S before expensive operations — check carefully with small counterexamples).

Derive the exact optimization: given initial sum S, a set P of indices to flip 0->1 (adds C_i after flip) and set Q of indices to flip 1->0 (subtracts C_i), find the ordering minimizing total cost; determine whether interleaving P and Q helps (e.g., removing large C first reduces S for subsequent operations).
Implement a brute-force solver (Dijkstra over 2^N states) for N <= 20 to validate the greedy formula on random small tests.
Run the validation script; if all tests pass, write the final O(N log N) solution reading from stdin and printing the answer.
Implement the final O(N log N) solution: compute S, partition differing indices, sort each group appropriately, simulate the order computing total cost with 64-bit integers.
Write a stress-test harness comparing brute force vs. greedy on thousands of random small cases, including cases where A==B and where extra flips might seem beneficial.
Finalize the Python solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin), careful handling of large answer magnitudes (up to ~2e5 * 2e11), and confirm against the provided samples.
